feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid public-sector experience. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by adding more outcome-based achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and communications leadership.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement strengthens trust and demonstrates increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost, or performance where possible.  
- Fix style consistency: punctuation and formatting vary (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. other compounds; “A2/Learning” is awkward). Consider “French (A2, learning).” Also “Coleman DAVIS” is stylistically inconsistent unless intentional branding.  

No major misspellings found; grammar is generally strong.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience bullets.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most relevant differentiators: public-sector scale, enterprise web modernization, and governance/analytics leadership.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, active phrasing such as “leading” or “modernizing” for stronger executive tone.
- Consider adding one concrete scale cue from recent roles (for example, high-volume or enterprise-scale) without repeating detailed metrics already covered in experience.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds and scales editorial systems, analytics infrastructure, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled digital experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is close to the subtitle and skills sections; simplify to avoid repetition.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but the section is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, executive-level wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure.”
- Replace vague phrases with clearer scope: change “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Multi-channel digital communications leadership.”
- Keep the strongest, most current differentiators: retain AI-enabled search, workflow automation/integrations, and public-sector/advocacy communications.
- Consider revised version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it to emphasize only the highest-value differentiators.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also reinforced in Work Experience and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like an extension of the experience section and repeats themes already covered elsewhere. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make the footer feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line label such as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Make descriptions more specific with differentiators: audience, platform, scale, or business purpose.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “Drupal 10,” and spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.
- Consider this tighter rewrite: AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery. We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future expansion.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely repeat current freelance bullets.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with NACo video/programming achievements in multiple roles.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Make it sharper by emphasizing this as a high-impact consulting engagement with 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship builds.

Suggested edit
- Open with the client, scope, and level: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-focused bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel operations.
- Add measurable signals where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/adoption, or workflow time saved.
- Use stronger verbs and specificity: “Built Drupal microsites and modular campaign templates,” “implemented front-end/CMS enhancements,” “designed retrieval and structured-content model for AI search.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats NACo Director and the summary; keep only if tied to a distinct consulting outcome.
- AI search and microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if channel oversight bullets emphasized outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget strategy for a national association serving county officials.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add email open/click growth, social engagement/follower growth, video output, event reach, or production cost/time savings if available.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards and cross-department workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; in this entry, emphasize enterprise leadership, platform modernization and systems-building.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep this version focused on organizational capability and scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item currently reads as a lighter version of the more senior NACo role above it. Tighten it around execution, cross-team coordination, and channel growth, with clearer outcomes if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct action: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or engagement if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams around more consistent digital production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating channel oversight, governance, and workflow language already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the earlier 2015–2018 NACo entry; differentiate this role as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for a more differentiated phrase like “Content operations & audience strategy” to sound more senior.
- Keep terminology consistent with recent roles: use “governance,” “operations,” and “enterprise” since those are strongly evidenced in 2022–present experience.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise web strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates “Digital governance & editorial systems” in Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is also repeated in Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work, with fewer low-signal platform names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages unless they are target-role keywords; they are less supported by recent experience.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with outcome-oriented language where possible: “enterprise CMS delivery,” “platform integration,” or “search and discovery.”
- Keep this section concise and let the Technical + IT section carry the full software inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies—use sharper wording here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, emphasize decision-making value and outcomes over platform names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy & reporting • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Web performance and SEO analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboarding” for clearer senior-level impact.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase tied to recent work, such as “analytics infrastructure for high-traffic public-sector websites” or “insight generation for enterprise web modernization.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here; move the full platform inventory to Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader web optimization language elsewhere; keep if SEO is a target keyword.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior-level wording:  
  **- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production**  
  **- Livestream and hybrid event production**  
  **- PTZ camera and studio system operation**  
  **- Virtual event and multi-camera production workflows**
- Consider swapping “Studio operations” for a more outcome-oriented phrase like **“studio buildout and production operations”** if you want to reflect the NACo in-house studio achievement.
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad categories (“video production”) with narrow tools (“PTZ camera systems”) unless all bullets are framed as capabilities.
- If possible elsewhere on the CV, attach scale/results to this area rather than listing more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- This section partially duplicates older NACo multimedia bullets, so keep it focused on current strategic production capability, not task-level execution.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section almost exactly. Use this space to signal depth and recency, with Drupal clearly leading.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (expert) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add brief context instead of a pure list: **Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider replacing weaker/less strategic items with capability framing: **Drupal architecture, CMS migrations, modular content systems, governance-oriented publishing**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; if “GitHub Pages” is minor exposure, move it to a lower-priority tools section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent roles/projects, so this section should add level/context, not just restate the keyword.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **Front-end & Technical Implementation:** HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they add little value and date the section.
- Consider replacing **jQuery** with **JavaScript/jQuery** only if it is still actively used in recent work; otherwise remove it to keep the list current.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier elsewhere in the CV tied to these tools, e.g., “used for microsite builds, tagging, automation, and lightweight edge/serverless deployments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- “API integrations” and broader technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies and recent work bullets.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already named elsewhere, so this item should be tighter and more function-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by category to show systems thinking, e.g.: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project and ticketing systems: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and stronger alignment with recent work.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one impact cue tied to recent roles, e.g. “used to support cross-department publishing, campaign coordination, and operational workflows.”
- Drop weaker/older-feeling tools if not current or central; keep the list focused on the platforms you actively use.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; listing both may add little unless collaboration platforms are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-level systems rather than repeat newsletter work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/scale: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: **Enterprise email automation, member communications, segmentation and journey orchestration across Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic and Mailchimp**
- If space is tight, keep only the strongest/current tools and move weaker/older ones to a broader “Additional Tools” line

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding campaign-volume claims here unless they are removed or sharpened there.
- “Engagement” is somewhat redundant with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; use platform-specific wording to differentiate.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Tighten it to emphasize platforms over broad capabilities, and only keep terms that add distinct technical value.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** if you want this to read as a tools stack; “SEO” is a capability, not a platform.
- Remove **Dashboarding** unless you specify a tool/context; it’s already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI.
- If space allows and it’s accurate, add one higher-signal item such as **KPI reporting**, **tagging/measurement strategy**, or **conversion analysis** instead of generic optimization language.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two sections.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating broad terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split broad claims into 2–3 specific achievements; e.g., “supported a major website refresh,” “produced livestreams and weekly video updates,” “coordinated day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of livestreams/videos, publishing cadence, audience growth, email volume, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and remove softer verbs like “contributed to” and “high-impact” unless backed by results.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and impact: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; produced digital and multimedia content to extend member engagement.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to” with stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “managed.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast first.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Since multimedia leadership already appears strongly in recent roles and Topline Skills, this item should stay concise, tool-focused, and avoid repeating broader production functions.

Suggested edit:
